claim: Broadcom specifies a 102.4T CPO switch with 512 x 200G all-optical I/O.
exact_wording: 512 x 200G PAM4 all-optical I/O
comparison_baseline: No architecture comparison
independent_support: CMP-002 and CMP-003 confirm the product description.
contradicting_evidence: No independent system verification reviewed.
notes: Product specification is credible for design intent but does not prove volume deployment.

claim: Arista demonstrated a 102.4T switch using advanced 1.6T pluggable optics.
exact_wording: 102.4 Tbps Switch; support for 200G-per-lane 1.6Tbps LPO, LRO and FRO
comparison_baseline: Broadcom 102.4T CPO path
independent_support: Official Arista event description.
contradicting_evidence: No detailed test report or production evidence reviewed.
notes: Demonstration supports technical plausibility only.

claim: A 102.4T aggregate switch capacity does not inherently require CPO.
comparison_baseline: CPO versus advanced pluggables at equal aggregate switch capacity
independent_support: Broadcom documents CPO and Arista reports pluggable operation at 102.4T.
contradicting_evidence: A live demo does not prove that the pluggable configuration is commercially viable at required power, cooling, reliability, and cost.
notes: Test by obtaining matched system data and production qualification evidence.

claim: Pluggable optics retain structural advantages in modularity, replacement, and supply-chain maturity.
exact_wording: Modularity; Reliability; Supply Chain Efficiency
comparison_baseline: CPO integrated service model
independent_support: OIF system-vendor requirements document.
contradicting_evidence: CPO may offer sufficient energy and density benefits to outweigh these advantages in selected domains.
notes: Advantage is structural; economic weight varies by deployment.

claim: CPO can reduce chip-to-module interface power and improve signal quality by shortening the electrical path and removing connectors.
exact_wording: reducing the length of this interface and the number of connectors
comparison_baseline: Faceplate pluggable chip-to-module channel
independent_support: OIF system-vendor requirements and CPO implementation agreement.
contradicting_evidence: The realised system-level benefit depends on architecture and comparison boundaries.
notes: Do not translate structural advantage into a percentage without matched measurement.

claim: Broadcom's 102.4T CPO commercial stage is not established as broad volume production by reviewed public evidence.
exact_wording: sampling to early access customers; Limited Release
comparison_baseline: Meaningful adoption requires repeat production or material revenue.
independent_support: Two official Broadcom sources provide bounded status language.
contradicting_evidence: Announcement headline uses shipping language.
notes: Require named deployment, repeat orders, units, or material revenue.

claim: No reviewed source provides a controlled all-in economic comparison of 102.4T CPO and advanced pluggables.
comparison_baseline: Matched port count, reach, workload, cooling boundary and reliability target
independent_support: Reviewed product and event materials omit the required complete comparison.
contradicting_evidence: A non-public customer study may exist.
notes: This is the main evidence gap.

claim: OIF identifies 5 pJ/bit as a target for back-end and other energy-sensitive interfaces, with some operators requesting 3 pJ/bit.
exact_wording: targeted power consumption is set at 5pJ/b with some operators calling for a 3pJ/b
comparison_baseline: Application-level requirement, not product measurement
independent_support: OIF requirements survey.
contradicting_evidence: Targets do not prove current product capability.
notes: Use as a target and scenario anchor only.

claim: Marvell reports less than 5 pJ/bit including laser power for a 1.6T LPO light engine under typical conditions.
exact_wording: consumes less than 5 picojoules per bit, including laser power, measured under typical operating conditions
comparison_baseline: CPO and fully retimed 1.6T interfaces
independent_support: Official Marvell announcement.
contradicting_evidence: No independent measurement or complete module and chassis boundary reviewed.
notes: Equivalent to less than 8 W at 1.6 Tb/s within the stated boundary.

claim: Marvell reports 22 W and 24 W demonstrations for 1.6T fully retimed optical modules.
exact_wording: 22 watts; 24 watts
comparison_baseline: LPO and CPO 1.6T interfaces
independent_support: Two official Marvell demonstration pages.
contradicting_evidence: Demonstration conditions and statistical production range are undisclosed.
notes: Use as scenario anchors, not a product-wide forecast.

claim: The central scenario estimates 601 W CPO, 668 W LPO, and 2004 W fully retimed switch-side optical facility power for 64 x 1.6T ports.
comparison_baseline: Common 102.4T switch-side boundary
independent_support: Formula audit in 08-model/102.4t-switch-side-power-model.md.
contradicting_evidence: No matched measured 102.4T chassis data; conversion and cooling are analyst assumptions.
notes: Do not cite these as observed product values.

claim: The modeled central CPO advantage over LPO is 10%, much smaller than its 70% advantage over fully retimed optics.
comparison_baseline: Facility-adjusted switch-side optical interface power
independent_support: Same-boundary formulas and shared overhead assumptions.
contradicting_evidence: CPO and LPO input boundaries are not measured in matched systems.
notes: The ranking can change if omitted CPO overhead exceeds 0.8 W per 1.6T port.

claim: NVIDIA is the provisional switch-platform CPO leader in reviewed public evidence, but CPO-specific deployment volume remains unverified.
comparison_baseline: Integrated switch, networking software, supply chain and customer adoption
independent_support: NVIDIA describes Spectrum-X Photonics as a production platform component and Meta confirms broad Spectrum-X adoption.
contradicting_evidence: Meta does not specify that its adopted systems are the CPO variant; no units or matched economics are disclosed.
notes: Leadership is category-specific and should not be generalized to lasers, merchant silicon or accelerator optical I/O.

claim: Broadcom has the strongest reviewed merchant-switch CPO maturity claim, including third-generation architecture and production-volume wording.
comparison_baseline: Merchant switch silicon and optical-engine integration
independent_support: Official product generations and OFC 2026 production-volume statement.
contradicting_evidence: No named customer, units, material CPO revenue or independent deployment evidence.
notes: Requires customer and revenue corroboration.

claim: Lumentum has the clearest reviewed near-term CPO economic signal among optical-component suppliers.
exact_wording: multi-hundred-million-dollar incremental CPO purchase order
comparison_baseline: Public order visibility and delivery timing
independent_support: Official financial-results disclosure.
contradicting_evidence: Customer, margins, order protections and final deployment are undisclosed.
notes: Track revenue conversion during the first half of calendar 2027.

claim: Coherent has the broadest reviewed public component and manufacturing stack for CPO, but its leadership claims lack independently verified shipped volume.
comparison_baseline: Laser, ELS, optical-engine, packaging and InP manufacturing breadth
independent_support: Official investor deck documents multiple layers of the stack and high-volume-order claims.
contradicting_evidence: Customer identity, order economics, qualification data, yields and CPO revenue are not disclosed.
notes: Compare with Lumentum on laser efficiency, qualified capacity, customer concentration and margins.

claim: Marvell provides a public-equity option on accelerator-side optical I/O after acquiring Celestial AI, but technology leadership is not yet demonstrated.
comparison_baseline: Accelerator scale-up optical I/O rather than switch-faceplate CPO
independent_support: Acquisition and financing facts are disclosed in the 10-Q.
contradicting_evidence: No comparable production, customer-volume, yield, reliability or economic evidence.
notes: Treat acquisition price and NVIDIA investment as strategic signals, not proof of technical superiority.

claim: Reviewed evidence is insufficient to name one company as the overall CPO technology and future-market leader.
comparison_baseline: Same product category, test boundary, reach, reliability target, production stage and economics
independent_support: The companies lead different layers and disclose non-comparable metrics.
contradicting_evidence: Vendor claims point to different leaders depending on category.
notes: Resolve with customer qualification, matched system tests, yield/rework, field reliability, unit economics and backlog conversion.

claim: Integration strategy is a first-order determinant of photonic-link performance, cost and manufacturability, with thermal pathways and manufacturing yield remaining near-term bottlenecks.
exact_wording: We identify near-term bottlenecks, notably thermal pathways and manufacturing yield
comparison_baseline: Isolated device performance versus complete integrated engine
independent_support: PAP-003 independently frames packaging, test, thermal management and manufacturability as system constraints.
contradicting_evidence: The review synthesises heterogeneous technologies and does not provide a matched production-yield comparison.
notes: Review-level synthesis; follow the underlying primary studies before assigning quantitative yield or cost effects.

claim: Wafer-level burn-in and testing can move laser reliability screening and calibration earlier in the manufacturing flow, but requires high-yield bonding and robust thermal pathways.
exact_wording: Wafer-scale burn-in and testing therefore become essential
comparison_baseline: Packaged-device screening after final assembly
independent_support: The review cites commercial scale for bonded III-V/silicon lasers and explains the manufacturing mechanism.
contradicting_evidence: No reviewed source yet quantifies CPO-engine yield improvement, cycle time or cost from this approach.
notes: Supports the view that test architecture and process control can be economically differentiating, but the profit effect is unquantified.

claim: PAP-024 reports that conventional uniform grating couplers are limited to approximately 2.2 dB loss and 30-40 nm bandwidth, while advanced grating and edge-coupler demonstrations can reach below 1 dB; some record couplers require process steps outside standard foundry flows.
exact_wording: Conventional uniform GCs are limited to ≈−2.2 dB ... edge couplers achieve <1 dB ... many record devices require process steps outside standard foundry flows
comparison_baseline: A qualified multi-fibre engine coupling-loss distribution and production-compatible process window
independent_support: The review cites multiple primary demonstrations and explicitly distinguishes conventional, advanced and non-standard process results.
contradicting_evidence: These are heterogeneous component results, not a matched package loss distribution, automated attach cycle time or production yield.
notes: Use to connect PIC design choices to packaging loss and manufacturing portability; do not treat a record coupler as a product specification.

claim: PAP-024 states that 2D wire-bond integration introduces approximately 0.5-1.0 nH/mm parasitics, restricts bandwidth below about 30 GHz in high-speed applications and typically has energy efficiency above 5 pJ/bit; this is a review synthesis, not a universal cutoff.
exact_wording: wire bonds introduce ... 0.5–1.0 nH mm−1 ... restricts bandwidth to <30 GHz ... 2D ... typically ... >5 pJ bit−1
comparison_baseline: A matched 2D package across a defined lane rate, equaliser and thermal boundary
independent_support: The review identifies the physical mechanism and cites prior demonstrations.
contradicting_evidence: The ranges depend on geometry, signalling, driver, package and comparison boundary; no current 200G/400G scale-out engine is benchmarked directly.
notes: Supports moving the benchmark beyond CPO labels to interconnect length, parasitics and power partition.

claim: PAP-024 describes 3D EIC-PIC integration as reducing interconnect length and parasitics, while advanced bump pitches of 10-40 µm and prototype 2 µm die-to-wafer bonding increase alignment and thermal-management demands that can reduce yield.
exact_wording: bump pitch ... 10–40 µm ... prototypes showing 2 µm die-to-wafer bonding ... sub-micrometre alignment tolerances that reduce yield
comparison_baseline: A production 3D optical engine with measured thermal cycling, alignment yield and rework economics
independent_support: The review distinguishes demonstrated bonding pitches from manufacturing and thermal constraints.
contradicting_evidence: No production yield, field reliability, package cost or qualification result is supplied; bonding and thermal claims are not a complete CPO business case.
notes: Treat fine-pitch 3D as a performance path whose economic value depends on test, thermal and yield closure.

claim: PAP-024 places mature pluggable optics at roughly 15-30 pJ/bit and describes LPO as reducing power by about 40% by removing module DSP, while citing a 2020 12.8T CPO demonstration with more than 30% power reduction; these are review-level, non-matched comparisons.
exact_wording: state-of-the-art modules ... around 15–30 pJ bit−1 ... LPO ... lowers power consumption by ~40% ... more than 30% reduction in power consumption
comparison_baseline: A current product-to-product chassis or engine comparison with identical reach, host, cooling, FEC and service boundaries
independent_support: The review cites underlying demonstrations and describes the architectural source of each reduction.
contradicting_evidence: The cited products, years, lane rates, power boundaries and workloads differ; no conclusion about current commercial superiority or margin follows.
notes: Use only as historical orientation; keep the project’s matched 102.4T scenario model as the quantitative comparison.

claim: PAP-014 describes a CMOS-compatible optical interposer with multiple optical waveguide layers, electrical traces/TSVs, integrated laser heat sinks, passive flip-chip placement guides and wafer-level assembly/test features.
exact_wording: CMOS compatible wafer fabrication methods ... multiple waveguide layers ... integrated heat sinks ... visually-assisted passive placement ... wafer scale passive assembly
comparison_baseline: A production wafer-scale interposer line with disclosed yield, Cpk, cycle time and cost
independent_support: The two-page paper describes the platform construction and assembly flow but does not provide production statistics.
contradicting_evidence: POET-authored conference digest; no independent manufacturing validation, lot distribution or customer qualification is reported.
notes: Use as a packaging/platform control-point hypothesis, not proof of HVM economics.

claim: PAP-014 reports measured waveguide loss below 0.3 dB/cm, 0.25 dB facet coupling loss, 0.5 dB vertical-mirror coupling loss and approximately 90% (1 dB) coupling efficiency for passively placed CW lasers.
exact_wording: material loss ... <0.3dB/cm ... facet coupling losses of 0.25dB ... 0.5dB coupling loss ... 90% (1dB) coupling efficiency
comparison_baseline: A complete engine optical-loss distribution over lots, temperature, wavelength and alignment state
independent_support: The paper reports component measurements and a passive-placement coupling result.
contradicting_evidence: The number of samples and distributions are not reported; results do not include the complete fibre-to-engine path or production rework/escape rate.
notes: Keep component loss separate from delivered engine-input power and final yield.

claim: PAP-014 demonstrates a 6 mm × 9 mm assembled engine containing four lasers, four high-speed photodetectors, four monitor photodiodes and a mux/demux pair; four such engines could fit in a QSFP-DD module according to the paper.
exact_wording: At 6mmx9mm ... incorporates 4 lasers, 4 high speed photodetectors, 4 monitor photo diodes and a multiplexer/de-multiplexer pair
comparison_baseline: A qualified 1.6T/3.2T module with measured aggregate performance and service data
independent_support: The paper provides an assembled-engine photograph and component count.
contradicting_evidence: The density statement is a physical fit claim; no multi-engine module, 200G-per-lane or 400G link, thermal cycling, yield or commercial volume is reported.
notes: Useful for package-density mapping; do not count four engines as a demonstrated QSFP-DD product.

claim: PAP-014 reports a 100G transmission eye and 100/200G receiver sensitivity results meeting 10 km LR4 requirements; the paper describes 400G as an extension with compatible photonics components rather than a measured 400G demonstration.
exact_wording: eye diagrams for 100G ... BER/Sensitivity performance of 100G/200G receivers ... meeting 10km LR4 ... readily extensible to 400G
comparison_baseline: A measured 400G aggregate or 200G/400G-per-lane engine link
independent_support: The paper separates the demonstrated 100G/200G results from the 400G extensibility statement.
contradicting_evidence: No BER count, lane-level 200G/400G result, full transmitter/receiver power, temperature, qualification or field data is supplied.
notes: Classify as a 100/200G component/engine demonstration, not current 400G readiness.

claim: PAP-014 claims wafer-scale assembly and test can reduce cost, while its modular pre-validated building blocks support passive integration; the economic benefit remains unquantified.
exact_wording: low cost through wafer scale assembly and test ... modular construction, with pre-validated building blocks
comparison_baseline: A measured cost-per-good-engine, yield curve, throughput and capex comparison versus hybrid package alternatives
independent_support: The paper states the proposed manufacturing mechanism and modular architecture.
contradicting_evidence: No wafer size, units per wafer, assembly cycle time, yield, scrap, capex, ASP or customer production evidence is reported.
notes: Use as a diligence hypothesis for POET/platform control, not a profit-pool conclusion.

claim: PAP-020 models a baseline 25.6 Tb/s spine/6.4 Tb/s leaf network with 272 switch ASICs and 12,288 endpoints against a 51.2 Tb/s CPO-enabled topology using 128-port, 400 Gb/s switches and optical server connectivity.
exact_wording: baseline ... 272 switch ASICs ... 12,288 end points ... proposed ... 51.2-Tb/s switches ... 128 ports ... 400 Gb/s per port
comparison_baseline: A deployed network comparison with matched hardware, cost, power, workload, service and availability
independent_support: The paper states the topology, oversubscription, port, bandwidth and endpoint assumptions.
contradicting_evidence: The configuration is a simulation scenario; it is not a customer architecture or a production CPO specification.
notes: Use to define a customer-level topology sensitivity, not to forecast switch units.

claim: Under PAP-020's modeled topology, the CPO-enabled network has 4× bisection bandwidth and 41% fewer switches than the baseline, with 112 fewer switches in the stated 12,288-endpoint configuration.
exact_wording: requires 112 fewer switches ... switch count reduction of 41% ... 4× increase in bisection BW
comparison_baseline: A measured and costed customer deployment showing the same switch-count and bisection change
independent_support: The result follows from the paper's specified topology and switch-radix assumptions.
contradicting_evidence: It excludes transition costs, procurement, service, optical-engine price, power/cooling capex and whether the workload needs the modeled topology.
notes: Treat as a system-value hypothesis; do not assign the saving to the CPO supplier.

claim: PAP-020's VM-trace simulation places large-scale applications under up to 50% fewer first-level switches in the CPO-enabled topology.
exact_wording: large-scale applications can be placed under up to 50% fewer first-level switches
comparison_baseline: A customer placement study using current production workload traces and an implemented CPO network
independent_support: The paper uses an Azure production VM trace and its stated placement model.
contradicting_evidence: The trace, placement policy, switch topology and availability assumptions are not a measured customer CPO outcome; the result may not generalize to AI training fabrics.
notes: Use to formulate workload-specific diligence questions, not an adoption-rate input.

claim: PAP-020's all-to-all discrete-event simulations report speedups up to 7.1 for the modeled 96-node/16 KiB case; normalized application execution-time reductions reach 23–26% at communication ratio 0.3 and 38.4–42.7% at ratio 0.5 across stated node/message cases.
exact_wording: greatest speedup equals 7.1 ... execution time reductions ... 26% and 42.7%
comparison_baseline: Measured application performance on matched CPO and baseline hardware
independent_support: The paper states simulator, traffic pattern, node counts, message sizes and communication-ratio calculations.
contradicting_evidence: Results are model-dependent and include topology, latency, buffer, routing and initialization assumptions; they do not establish revenue, TCO or customer willingness to pay.
notes: Keep performance benefit separate from optical-engine supplier economics.

claim: PAP-020 cites estimated CPO power reductions of 25–50% and up to 50% lower system cost per capacity at a 10–15 pJ/bit target, but these are cited estimates rather than measurements in the paper's network simulation.
exact_wording: reductions of 25% to 50% ... up to 50% system-level reduction in the cost per capacity ... 10–15 pJ/bit
comparison_baseline: A matched current CPO-versus-pluggable system cost and power study with complete boundary and supplier prices
independent_support: The paper labels the figures as estimates and cites prior work.
contradicting_evidence: No engine ASP, package yield, service cost, cooling, capex or supplier margin is included; do not use the figures as a current product forecast.
notes: Historical orientation only; use the project's 102.4T power model for quantitative comparisons.

claim: PAP-023 explains that representing a multiwavelength, multimode photonic signal as an electrical equivalent can require up to a nine-fold increase in electrical ports and signals per wavelength, creating pin-count, probing and verification complexity.
exact_wording: up to a nine-fold increase per wavelength in the number of electrical ports and signals
comparison_baseline: A measured production-design productivity or verification-failure comparison across EDA flows
independent_support: The paper provides the signal-representation mapping and its consequences for PIC design.
contradicting_evidence: The nine-fold figure is a representation example, not a universal factor for every PIC or PDK; no production benchmark is reported.
notes: Use to identify design-tool bottleneck potential, not to infer software revenue or engine yield.

claim: PAP-023 argues that native domain-specific electronic and photonic circuit simulators with common sampling grids avoid the overhead and error-prone port expansion of treating photonics as electronics.
exact_wording: domain-specific simulators ... eliminates expensive trade-offs ... sampled on a common grid ... without additional computational overheads
comparison_baseline: A controlled tapeout, design-cycle or verification-quality comparison against an electrical-only flow
independent_support: The paper describes automatic partitioning of electrical and photonic subcircuits and shared waveform probing.
contradicting_evidence: The paper is a Synopsys-authored method demonstration and supplies no independent user study, time saving, software pricing or production tapeout data.
notes: Treat as a tooling hypothesis; retain Synopsys as an adjacent platform candidate, not an optical-engine leader.

claim: In PAP-023's TW-MZM example, a Q-factor of 8 tolerates an RF path-length mismatch up to 21 mm at 10 Gb/s and only 8 mm at 25 Gb/s for the studied PIC and model.
exact_wording: to guarantee a Q-factor of 8 ... 21mm ... at 10Gbps ... 8mm ... at 25Gbps
comparison_baseline: A measured high-speed CPO PIC with matched packaging, electrical loss, temperature and Q/BER boundary
independent_support: The paper plots Q-factor versus path-length mismatch in a specific co-simulation example.
contradicting_evidence: This is a design-specific simulation result; it is not a universal 200G/400G package tolerance or a product qualification limit.
notes: Use to show why package layout and E-O co-design interact; do not extrapolate the millimetre limits to lane-rate forecasts.

claim: PAP-023 supports the inference that EDA/PDK interoperability and automatic E-O partitioning could become a scalable control point as PIC component counts grow, but it does not establish a durable software profit pool.
exact_wording: component count ... rapidly growing ... rethinking ... E-O co-design ... scalable, tractable, intuitive and faithful
comparison_baseline: Recurring software revenue, foundry PDK adoption, customer design wins and measurable tapeout productivity
independent_support: The paper is a design-flow proposal and example from Synopsys authors.
contradicting_evidence: No customer, pricing, adoption, independent benchmark, gross margin or link-performance evidence is reported.
notes: Track as an adjacent supplier/control-point hypothesis only.

claim: NWS-001 is a secondary orientation source that frames 200G electrical SerDes reach and CPO reliability/serviceability as adoption issues; it does not itself establish a measured 200G link, production CPO ramp or customer deployment.
exact_wording: With 200G electrical SerDes, we have arrived at a limit in terms of reach ... main issue of CPO is reliability and serviceability
comparison_baseline: A primary measured 200G system result or customer production/service record
independent_support: The newsletter's framing is directionally consistent with the project’s reviewed LPO/CPO sources.
contradicting_evidence: The post supplies no reproducible test boundary, units, customer, qualification, field-return or cost data and includes opinionated forecasts.
notes: Use only to prioritize primary-source checks; never cite as the technical or commercial proof.

claim: NWS-001 itself notes that optical-company proprietary-edge claims are difficult to verify; this supports a diligence rule requiring matched performance, qualification, content and margin evidence before ranking Lumentum, Coherent or other suppliers.
exact_wording: I have no way of verifying any of these claims ... very difficult to form an opinion
comparison_baseline: A matched independent supplier comparison with production and financial evidence
independent_support: The post explicitly distinguishes its investment opinion from verifiable company evidence.
contradicting_evidence: This is an author observation, not independent evidence that any specific supplier lacks an edge.
notes: Use as a process reminder, not a negative claim about a company.

claim: NWS-001 mentions Ayar Labs financing and rumors of future NVIDIA use; only the official financing announcement is eligible for evidence, while the deployment rumor remains unverified and excluded from the scorecard.
exact_wording: Ayar Labs just raised a new round ... rumors about Nvidia actually using it in 2026/2027
comparison_baseline: Customer-confirmed Ayar/NVIDIA production deployment and product boundary
independent_support: The newsletter links to an official Ayar financing page but does not provide customer evidence for the rumor.
contradicting_evidence: Financing is not deployment; the post is secondary and contains no units, qualification, product ASP or revenue evidence.
notes: Track the official financing separately; do not convert this article into a customer or revenue claim.

claim: NWS-002 reports that Broadcom presented CPO reliability data showing zero failures over approximately one million device-hours and an asserted statistical MTBF boundary; this remains unverified secondary reporting until the original presentation and test definition are retained.
exact_wording: Broadcom actually got ZERO FAILURES in this 1M device hours of data ... 2.5-million-hour MTBF
comparison_baseline: A retained Broadcom primary reliability presentation with population, stress, censoring, confidence and FEC/BER boundaries
independent_support: The newsletter identifies the reported device-hour observation and its uncertainty, but does not supply the original slide deck or methods.
contradicting_evidence: Secondary report; no sample definition, temperature, acceleration model, confidence interval or independent customer/field data is available.
notes: Do not enter the reliability benchmark or company scorecard until the primary source is recovered.

claim: NWS-002 argues that external, serviceable lasers can isolate a failure-prone light-source domain, but complete CPO reliability still depends on PIC, photodiode, fibre attach, package and control failures.
exact_wording: CPO ... external lasers ... PLUGGABLE ... fewer points of failure ... CPO ... more reliable
comparison_baseline: A matched field-reliability comparison for ELSFP CPO and pluggable engines across all failure modes
independent_support: The article’s mechanism is consistent with the project’s external-light and packaging boundaries.
contradicting_evidence: The newsletter supplies no FMEA, field-return population, service cost or matched baseline; “intrinsically” is not accepted as a universal conclusion.
notes: Use as a prompt to recover primary FMEA/field data, not as reliability proof.

claim: NWS-002 reports sparse public quantitative Marvell CPO disclosure at OCP and expresses skepticism about broad 400G electrical-SerDes feasibility; these are conference observations and author opinions, not product findings.
exact_wording: Marvell showed literally zero data ... 400G PAM4 ... not going to work for most channels
comparison_baseline: Marvell’s retained conference material and measured 400G channel evidence with stated loss, return-loss, crosstalk and BER boundaries
independent_support: The recap reports what the author says was shown or not shown at the event.
contradicting_evidence: No independent event record or complete Marvell product presentation is retained; the 400G opinion conflicts with the need for matched measurements.
notes: Keep Marvell’s maturity state based on primary company and paper evidence only.

claim: NWS-002 raises the hypothesis that high-lane-count BERT and signal-integrity test equipment can materially improve complex AI-rack/backplane yield, but the claimed yield improvement is not independently evidenced in the source.
exact_wording: Multilane helped the ecosystem dramatically improve yields (80-90%) ... giant 64-lane BERT
comparison_baseline: A customer or rack-integrator yield waterfall showing test insertion, escape-rate reduction, cycle time and cost per good assembly
independent_support: The article describes a plausible test-control mechanism and cites equipment capabilities informally.
contradicting_evidence: No retained customer data, lot counts, baseline definition, or causal test intervention is supplied.
notes: Track as a packaging/test diligence question; do not credit a vendor with yield leadership.

claim: Nokia fabricated an eight-channel monolithic InP transmitter PIC integrating four DFB lasers, eight MZMs, eight SOAs and eight power-monitor taps.
exact_wording: Monolithic PIC Architecture comprises 4 DFBs, 8 MZMs, 8 SOAs, and 8 taps with power monitors
comparison_baseline: Discrete or hybrid laser, modulator and amplifier assemblies
independent_support: Complete OFC paper reports the architecture and DC testing of all eight channels.
contradicting_evidence: The paper does not report production yield, die size, cost, lifetime or volume-manufacturing statistics.
notes: Direct device evidence for a vertically integrated transmitter architecture; commercial maturity remains unproven.

claim: A representative channel of Nokia's InP transmitter demonstrated 106.25-GBd PAM4 linear-drive operation at 60 C with about 3 dB TDECQ, about 0.97 RLM, about 3.5 dB outer extinction ratio and roughly 3-5 dBm fibre-coupled output.
exact_wording: RLM ~0.97, outer ER ~3.5 dB, TDECQ ~3dB, and average fiber coupled power ~3 to ~5 dBm
comparison_baseline: 200G-per-lane transmitter performance under a defined laboratory boundary
independent_support: The abstract and conclusion agree with the page-three measurement summary.
contradicting_evidence: Only one representative channel received reported RF characterisation; both transmitter and receiver used 15-tap FFE and no complete link-power figure is supplied.
notes: Measured device result, not proof of an eight-channel qualified optical engine.

claim: When packaged in an OSFP LPO configuration, all eight Nokia transmitter channels produced 2.8-3.0 dBm modulated average output, but full RF optimisation and reporting remained future work.
exact_wording: Driving the OSFP in 106 GBd PAM4 on all 8 channels produced modulated average output powers in the range of 2.8-3.0 dBm
comparison_baseline: Single-channel RF probe versus an assembled eight-channel LPO module
independent_support: The paper separately reports DC testing across all channels and a representative-channel RF result.
contradicting_evidence: No eight-channel BER, TDECQ distribution, reach, power, thermal, reliability or qualification result is reported for the packaged configuration.
notes: Important boundary: optical output across eight channels is not equivalent to full eight-channel link validation.

claim: The reviewed Nokia result does not establish total optical-engine power, final-package yield, qualification, field reliability, production volume or total cost.
exact_wording: RF set-up, optimization and reporting will follow
comparison_baseline: Qualification-ready and manufacturable 1.6T optical engine
independent_support: The paper explicitly limits reported RF performance to one representative channel and provides no production statistics.
contradicting_evidence: Additional non-public or later Nokia evidence may exist.
notes: These unknowns prevent the result from supporting a company-leadership or profit-pool conclusion.

claim: A modeled 224 Gb/s O-band QAM-16 coherent transmitter reaches an optimum 2.27 pJ/bit unequalised, 1.63 pJ/bit with one-tap transmitter FFE and 1.35 pJ/bit with one-tap host-SerDes DFE under the paper's stated assumptions.
exact_wording: The unequalized link shows an optimum TX energy-efficiency of 2.27 pJ/bit which improves down to 1.35 pJ/bit with a 1-tap DFE and 1.63 pJ/bit with a 1-tap FFE
comparison_baseline: Measured complete-link power for an equivalent reach and BER boundary
independent_support: Peer-reviewed closed-form framework incorporates driver and MZM bandwidth, laser splitting, receiver sensitivity and equalisation response.
contradicting_evidence: It is a modeled design point, not a fabricated 224 Gb/s link; parameter assumptions include 10% laser wall-plug efficiency and a 3 dB link margin.
notes: The abstract reports rounded values of 2, 1.4 and 1.2 pJ/bit; retain the detailed Section V values for reproducibility.

claim: PAP-012's energy result is not a full-link or system power figure because it optimises driver plus wall-plug-adjusted laser energy while excluding host-SerDes energy, receiver energy, bias circuits and thermal phase shifters.
exact_wording: estimating the energy efficiency of the host SerDes ... is beyond the purview of this work
comparison_baseline: Full optical-link energy including host electrical interfaces, transmitter, receiver, laser, tuning and control
independent_support: The paper explicitly defines the co-optimisation scope and separately identifies static bias and thermal-phase-shifter power.
contradicting_evidence: A compatible product could report a different boundary, so comparison requires component-by-component reconciliation.
notes: Prevents a false comparison with module-level or wall-plug system power.

claim: The coherent model finds a joint optimum rather than a monotonic device rule: stronger drivers reduce required laser power until driver power dominates, and MZM-length benefit saturates around 1 mm under the selected parameters.
exact_wording: the achievable energy-efficiency initially improves with increase in MZM length, the improvement saturates after a certain length (~1mm)
comparison_baseline: Selecting the individually best laser, driver or modulator metric
independent_support: The paper sweeps driver transconductance, laser power, split ratio, shunt resistance and MZM length within one framework.
contradicting_evidence: The optimum is conditional on modeled component values, reach assumptions and energy-accounting boundary, not universal across platforms.
notes: Supports system co-design as a diligence requirement without establishing a commercial winner.

claim: Lightmatter measured a monolithic microring Tx+Rx in GF 45SPCLO operating at 56 Gb/s NRZ without equalisation in 0.006 mm2 total active area, with 84.4 mW power excluding the laser or 1.51 pJ/bit.
exact_wording: Our Tx and Rx had a power consumption of 84.4 mW (excluding the laser), translating to an efficiency of 1.51 pJ/bit at 56 Gbps
comparison_baseline: Matched 200G-per-lane multi-wavelength optical engine
independent_support: The paper reports device spectra, bandwidths, eye measurements and a state-of-the-art comparison table.
contradicting_evidence: Single-wavelength on-chip link using an off-chip laser, external supplies and PRBS9; the heater-power boundary is not specified and no fibre reach is tested.
notes: Strong density result, but its lane rate and test boundary differ materially from a 1.6T scale-out engine.

claim: Lightmatter's 64 Gb/s result required three-tap receiver FFE applied in oscilloscope software and used inferred BER below 1e-12 because direct BER measurement was unavailable.
exact_wording: Direct BER measurements using a BER tester were not possible due to instrumentation limitations
comparison_baseline: 56 Gb/s open eye without equalisation and a direct error-counted 64 Gb/s result
independent_support: The paper distinguishes raw and equalised eyes and explains the measurement limitation.
contradicting_evidence: The paper says further measurement results would be presented at the conference; no later record has yet been reviewed.
notes: Do not cite 64 Gb/s as an unequalised or directly error-counted result.

claim: PAP-021 does not establish a packaged multi-wavelength engine, 200G-per-lane performance, fibre reach, production yield, qualification or commercial economics.
exact_wording: compatible with 200 GHz spacing 8-lambda WDM
comparison_baseline: Qualified scale-out optical engine
independent_support: The demonstrated circuit is single-wavelength and the Tx and Rx are connected by an on-chip waveguide.
contradicting_evidence: Future or non-public Lightmatter product evidence may address these gaps.
notes: Architecture compatibility is not equivalent to an eight-wavelength system demonstration.

claim: Ayar's early MOLA proof of concept uses a 12-fibre connector described as scalable to 24; simulations give 0.2 dB-penalty tolerances of 6 um translation, +/-0.2 degrees tilt and +/-600 um separation, while ten mating cycles showed less than 0.1 dB repeatability standard deviation.
exact_wording: The standard deviation of the repeatability test is less than 0.1 dB, based on early proof-of-concept samples
comparison_baseline: Qualified connector performance across production lots, environmental stress and lifetime cycles
independent_support: The paper provides connector geometry, tolerance simulations and per-channel repeatability data.
contradicting_evidence: Tolerance values are simulated; the repeatability sample count is undisclosed and ten cycles are insufficient for reliability or high-volume claims.
notes: Separate simulated alignment tolerance from measured short-cycle repeatability.

claim: Ayar proposes testing the fibre-attached optical I/O chiplet electrically and optically before final multi-chip-package assembly to avoid combining fibre-attach loss with the yield risk of expensive compute components.
exact_wording: the photonic chip is connectorized with a fiber attachment process and tested before being integrated into a multi-chip package
comparison_baseline: Fibre attach after final package assembly
independent_support: The paper supplies a specific wafer-sort, die-prep, fibre-attach, KGCC-test and final-assembly process sequence.
contradicting_evidence: No comparative yield, scrap cost, cycle time, rework, field reliability or volume data demonstrate the economic benefit.
notes: A credible manufacturing mechanism, not evidence that Ayar has achieved superior production economics.

claim: Lumentum's packaged 1310 nm DFB prototype delivered maximum ex-fibre powers of 720, 640 and 580 mW at laser temperatures of 25, 40 and 50 C, respectively, with 86% fibre-coupling efficiency.
exact_wording: The maximum output powers are 720mW, 640mW, and 580mW at 25 C, 40 C, and 50 C laser diode temperatures, respectively
comparison_baseline: Packaged external laser at defined fibre and temperature boundary
independent_support: The complete two-page paper reports both chip-on-submount and 14-pin butterfly-module measurements across laser and case temperatures.
contradicting_evidence: Single prototype result; the paper provides no sample distribution, aging, reliability, yield or production data.
notes: The chip-on-submount reached 880 mW at 25 C; do not substitute that for packaged ex-fibre power.

claim: At 400 mW ex-fibre output, Lumentum's prototype maintained at least 10% module power-conversion efficiency across the reported test conditions, with module SMSR above 45 dB and RINc below -156 dBc over 200-500 mW at 40 and 50 C laser temperature.
exact_wording: At 400mW ex-fiber power, the module PCE is at least 10% at all the testing conditions
comparison_baseline: High-power ELS electrical-to-fibre efficiency and spectral quality
independent_support: The paper reports module current-voltage-power, temperature sweeps, spectra and fibre-coupling efficiency.
contradicting_evidence: The RINc unit and integration boundary are not fully explained in the digest; no reflector, lifetime or multi-channel ELS test is provided.
notes: Useful module-boundary result, but not a complete ELSFP or system power measurement.

claim: Sumitomo's SOA-integrated 1.3 um DFB laser produced more than 500 mW at 45 C and more than 300 mW at 70 C, with reported 25% PCE over 200-440 mW at 45 C, SMSR above 50 dB and linewidth below 200 kHz.
exact_wording: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) at 45 C is 25% with optical power range from 200 to 440 mW
comparison_baseline: Packaged ex-fibre high-power ELS performance
independent_support: The one-page paper provides the device structure and light-output curves over temperature.
contradicting_evidence: Output is not identified as fibre-coupled; PCE boundary, sample size, packaging and test details are sparse; no lifetime, yield or cost evidence is reported.
notes: Device-level evidence for a strong alternative high-power InP architecture.

claim: The reviewed evidence cannot establish whether Lumentum's conventional high-power DFB or Sumitomo's SOA-integrated DFB has superior efficiency because their power and efficiency boundaries are not matched.
comparison_baseline: Same fibre-coupled output, laser and case temperature, package, drive electronics, spectral requirement and aging state
independent_support: Both papers report high power across temperature, and each discloses a PCE result.
contradicting_evidence: Lumentum reports a packaged ex-fibre module; Sumitomo does not state a fibre-coupled boundary or sufficiently define the PCE calculation.
notes: Do not rank suppliers by comparing 10% and 25% directly.

claim: A polymer 1x4 splitter distributed more than +20 dBm per ELS channel without a visible high-power loss increase and supported 112 Gb/s PAM4 measurements below 3.4 dB TDECQ on every tested output and CWDM4 wavelength.
exact_wording: we confirmed that even when +20 dBm is input, the loss characteristic shows almost no change
comparison_baseline: Silicon-waveguide branching and direct fibre distribution
independent_support: The two-page paper shows the splitter-loss plot, sixteen eye diagrams and sixteen TDECQ points.
contradicting_evidence: Each wavelength and output was measured sequentially with an external modulator and sampling scope; no BER, reach or simultaneous multi-output link is reported.
notes: Demonstrates high-power tolerance and signal quality, not a complete optical engine.

claim: The PAP-026 splitter prototype incurred approximately 10.5-15 dB total insertion loss, materially above the ideal 6 dB four-way division, and required a bismuth-doped fibre amplifier in the experiment.
exact_wording: A bismuth-doped fiber amplifier (BDFA) amplifies the optical signal to compensate for splitter losses
comparison_baseline: Low-loss passive external-laser fan-out
independent_support: Approximate insertion-loss range is read from the paper's Figure 2; the authors attribute excess loss to fabrication errors and state the amplifier could be removed if loss improves.
contradicting_evidence: Plot-derived range rather than tabulated values; future fabrication could materially reduce loss.
notes: Evidence that ELS distribution loss and amplification can offset headline source power and efficiency.

claim: PAP-026 directly demonstrates 400 Gb/s potential through one ELS wavelength and a 1x4 splitter; its 1.6 Tb/s and 3.2 Tb/s figures are extrapolations to four and eight ELS channels, not simultaneous aggregate transmission results.
exact_wording: potentially achieved 1.6 Tbps by employing 4 channels of ELS ... possibility extends to 3.2 Tbps transmission for all 8 channels
comparison_baseline: Simultaneous multi-wavelength, multi-output aggregate link
independent_support: The conclusion explicitly distinguishes the demonstrated one-channel result from the projected channel multiplication.
contradicting_evidence: No system test exercises all ELS channels and splitter outputs concurrently.
notes: Prevents the abstract's 3.2 Tb/s language from being treated as measured aggregate capacity.

claim: A five-micrometre-aperture 850 nm Zn-diffusion VCSEL produced 6.7 mW quasi-single-mode output, 27 GHz E-O bandwidth and 56 Gb/s eye patterns that remained visually open under -6 dB optical feedback.
exact_wording: invariant 56 Gbps eye patterns under strong optical feedback (-6 dB)
comparison_baseline: 200G-per-lane O-band CPO source at package temperature
independent_support: The journal paper reports L-I curves, spectra, frequency response and controlled reflector eye tests.
contradicting_evidence: Single laboratory device; eye pattern rather than direct BER measurement; no package-temperature, array, lifetime, yield or qualification evidence.
notes: The 6.7 mW and 27 GHz results belong to the five-micrometre aperture variant.

claim: A separate seven-micrometre-aperture VCSEL variant reached 16 mW near-single-mode output with 26 dB SMSR and 18 GHz E-O bandwidth, so the paper's maximum power and maximum bandwidth are not one operating point.
exact_wording: under a 12 mA bias current, the VCSEL can reach a nearly SM output with a 26 dB SMSR and 16 mW maximum output power
comparison_baseline: Five-micrometre high-speed device and a single combined best-case specification
independent_support: Figures 4 and 5 report the two aperture variants separately.
contradicting_evidence: Near-single-mode behaviour changes with bias and the authors identify mode stability as future work.
notes: Do not combine 16 mW with the 27 GHz or 56 Gb/s result.

claim: The five-micrometre VCSEL produced stated error-free eye patterns at 46 Gb/s over 500 m OM4 MMF and 48 Gb/s over 200 m nominal SMF without equalisation, with about 25% optical coupling in the SMF experiment.
exact_wording: clear and error-free eye patterns can be successfully achieved at 48 Gbit/sec through 200 meter SMF transmission
comparison_baseline: Back-to-back eye and direct error-counted BER over a standard single-mode link
independent_support: The paper provides eye diagrams for both reaches and explains that the nominal SMF is two-mode at 850 nm.
contradicting_evidence: No BER counter, threshold or confidence interval is reported; 'error-free' is based on eye-pattern presentation. The 850 nm link boundary differs from O-band scale-out engines.
notes: Treat as an eye-diagram transmission result, not quantified BER evidence.

claim: The reviewed VCSEL result does not establish a VCSEL array, 200G-per-lane performance, packaged engine, thermal distribution, lifetime, manufacturing yield, cost or qualification.
comparison_baseline: Qualification-ready scale-out optical engine
independent_support: The paper is a complete peer-reviewed single-device study and explicitly identifies future mode-stability work.
contradicting_evidence: Commercial or later system evidence may exist but is not supplied by this paper.
notes: VCSEL remains a longer-term short-reach integrated-source countercase, not a current matched rival to high-power InP ELS.

claim: IBM assembled 30 sixteen-channel passive fibre-array-attach mock-ups and used 1,178 observations to build a four-factor OBR model with reported correlation 0.98, average prediction error 0.4 dB and error standard deviation 0.5 dB.
exact_wording: The evaluation of the error is performed reinjecting the same input parameters dataset into the model
comparison_baseline: Independent held-out validation of loopback-free insertion-loss prediction
independent_support: The paper provides the test vehicles, loopback reference measurements, extracted OBR factors and model-error plot.
contradicting_evidence: The same input data were reinjected for evaluation, so the reported fit does not establish out-of-sample false-pass or false-fail performance.
notes: Use as process-monitoring feasibility evidence, not a validated production classifier or yield result.

claim: The IBM comparison estimates GLP at ten seconds setup plus two minutes measurement per sixteen-channel site, versus one minute setup plus three to ten minutes measurement for either OBR or standard insertion loss; GLP was only a process-drift screen and required more statistics for quantitative loss prediction.
exact_wording: An accurate IL value prediction based only on GLP measurements seems to be difficult to obtain
comparison_baseline: Standard loopback IL measurement on a functional CPO site
independent_support: Table II compares loopback compatibility, sensitivity, in-line use, setup and measurement duration across all three methods.
contradicting_evidence: Cycle times are study estimates rather than audited line-throughput distributions, and transfer to other couplers remains untested.
notes: Potential die-area and test-time benefit, but not evidence of lower cost per good engine.

claim: PAP-015 does not report fibre-attach first-pass yield, Cpk, rework, scrap cost, production volume or cross-line model transfer, so its claim of HVM compatibility does not establish achieved high-volume economics.
exact_wording: compatible with the high-volume manufacturing of co-packaged optics
comparison_baseline: Audited production output and cost per qualified attach
independent_support: The study uses process-of-record and deliberately misaligned mock-ups to test monitoring methods.
contradicting_evidence: Commercial IBM or OSAT data could address the missing manufacturing boundary but are not present in the paper.
notes: Separate tooling/process compatibility from actual qualified volume.

claim: A finite-element model of a 200 x 200 mm 51.2T CPO assembly with sixteen 3.2T socketed optical engines produced socket-area warpage of 0.035 and 0.041 mm, corner-BGA stress of about 38 MPa after cooling and 41 MPa after 400 N compression, and socket corner forces of 0.21-0.23 N.
exact_wording: The evaluation results meet the process targets during the assembly of the CPO
comparison_baseline: Physical measurements on assembled and cycled 51.2T packages
independent_support: The paper states targets of below 0.05 mm warpage, below the approximately 75 MPa SAC305 yield reference and above 0.1 N terminal force.
contradicting_evidence: All values are simulation outputs under stated material equivalence, symmetry and reference-temperature assumptions.
notes: The results show conditional assembly feasibility, not package qualification.

claim: The modeled package has a mechanical trade-off: increasing stiffener width reduced substrate warpage but raised C4 stress materially above 15 mm, while the selected 5 mm 34-layer PCB cut modeled warpage to about half that of the 2 mm HDI board at slightly higher BGA stress.
exact_wording: when the stiffener ring width exceeded 15 mm, the maximum equivalent stress of the C4 bump increased significantly
comparison_baseline: A package design that monotonically improves all stress and flatness metrics
independent_support: The paper sweeps stiffener width and three substrate designs under the same model.
contradicting_evidence: Cost is discussed qualitatively, the global solder model is simplified and no hardware confirms the optimum.
notes: Supports coupled package optimisation rather than selecting a single best flatness metric.

claim: PAP-016 does not establish physical reflow yield, repeated-cycle fatigue, optical alignment retention, environmental qualification or field reliability because it is a simulation study that assumes an initially flat substrate and omits fibre optics and passive components.
exact_wording: the actual warpage includes the substrate factory warpage, while the simulation assumes that the substrate is initially flat
comparison_baseline: Measured qualification and lifetime distribution for the proposed assembly
independent_support: The authors disclose model simplifications, equivalent materials and the initially flat boundary.
contradicting_evidence: Future hardware validation may support the model, but none is reported in this paper.
notes: Do not compare the 38-41 MPa modeled stress directly with an observed lifetime or failure rate.

claim: Corning's sixteen-channel glass fan-out converted 250 um pitch to 50 um pitch with average fibre-to-fibre insertion loss of 0.86 +/- 0.13 dB, including two estimated 0.3 dB edge couplings, 0.126 dB propagation loss and 0.14 +/- 0.13 dB bend loss.
exact_wording: The total insertion loss (fiber-to-fiber) yields an average of 0.86 +/- 0.13 dB
comparison_baseline: Complete detachable fibre-to-PIC path
independent_support: The paper reports all sixteen channels and reconciles the modeled and measured loss components.
contradicting_evidence: The fan-out result excludes the separate evanescent PIC interface and detachable connector.
notes: A useful distribution-level subassembly result with an explicit loss boundary.

claim: Across six flip-chip SiN devices, Corning's best reported partial-path loss was 0.38 dB at 1337 nm; the result included glass bend, propagation and evanescent coupling but excluded FAU-to-glass edge coupling, while a separate detachable connector interface reported 0.8 dB.
exact_wording: Not included is the edge coupling loss of FAU to IOX waveguide
comparison_baseline: One combined detachable fibre-to-PIC assembly at 1310 nm
independent_support: The paper states the six-device boundary and defines the included loss components.
contradicting_evidence: The 0.38 dB minimum and 0.8 dB connector result come from separate sub-experiments and cannot be treated as one demonstrated path.
notes: Prevents best partial-path results from being presented as complete engine coupling loss.

claim: Corning states that work was still ongoing to combine its evanescent and detachable interfaces; PAP-017 supplies no mating-cycle, reflow, environmental, yield, cost or volume evidence.
exact_wording: Additional work is ongoing to combine both interfaces and demonstrate the full low-loss glass interconnect solution
comparison_baseline: Qualified complete glass interconnect
independent_support: The summary explicitly identifies combination of the interfaces as future work.
contradicting_evidence: Later Corning evidence may close the gap but is not included in this paper.
notes: Classify as promising component evidence, not a qualification-ready connector platform.

claim: Furukawa measured two twelve-channel FA-to-FA connector pairs at 1310 nm over ten mating cycles, with insertion loss at or below 0.4 dB and cycle variation within +/-0.05 dB.
exact_wording: Low insertion loss <= 0.4 dB with small variation within +/- 0.05 dB is demonstrated in 10 cycles connections
comparison_baseline: Connector lifetime and production-lot distribution
independent_support: The complete paper shows all twelve channels for both samples over all ten cycles.
contradicting_evidence: Two connector pairs and ten cycles are insufficient for wear, environmental or production-reliability inference.
notes: Short-cycle laboratory repeatability only.

claim: Furukawa exposed one PLC assembly with its fibre-side connectors removed to one 260 C peak lasting 60 seconds; total pre-reflow loss was below 1 dB, average before/after change was below 0.14 dB and five-cycle variation before and after remained within +/-0.05 dB.
exact_wording: the temperature profile with peak temperature of 260 C and 60 seconds duration is applied as a condition close to reflow
comparison_baseline: JEDEC or customer qualification on a populated CPO substrate
independent_support: The paper identifies the PLC proxy, one-sample boundary, loss composition and before/after procedure.
contradicting_evidence: It does not specify a complete reflow profile, multiple thermal exposures, populated CPO package, sample distribution or environmental sequence.
notes: A reflow-feasibility screen, not proof of reflow qualification or lifetime.

claim: Furukawa demonstrated a four-connector glass-substrate mock-up with twelve-channel connectors at 10 mm spacing, equivalent to 1.2 channels/mm, but did not test a powered PIC or optical engine in that assembly.
exact_wording: we mocked up four series connection of FAs to glass substrate with high packaging density of 1.2 channel/mm
comparison_baseline: Functional multi-engine CPO package with qualified connector density
independent_support: The complete paper shows the physical before/after connector mock-up.
contradicting_evidence: No optical performance, assembly yield, thermal interaction, signal integrity, service procedure, cost or production data are reported for the four-connector mock-up.
notes: Geometry demonstration only.

claim: Meta measured two preliminary 100G-per-lane LPO designs in a 51.2T switch across chip-to-module EIC back-to-back loss as high as 15 dB at 26 GHz; most port/module combinations showed a BER floor of 1e-9, while LPO1 degraded as high as 1e-7.
exact_wording: Most of the LPO designs had a BER floor of 1E-9, and LPO1 had degradation up to 1E-7
comparison_baseline: Qualified production multi-vendor 100G LPO deployment
independent_support: The paper separates the 100G measured switch experiment from its 200G simulation and reports loss, TDECQ, sensitivity and BER-floor outcomes.
contradicting_evidence: Preliminary designs; no field duration, qualification, customer, module-power or service statistics; one design showed a materially poorer BER floor.
notes: Direct system evidence at 100G, not proof of universal interoperability or commercial maturity.

claim: In Meta's modeled 200G-per-lane CWDM4 case, linear LPO needs about 22 dB channel loss to meet the stated receiver sensitivity and less than 23 dB to meet transmitter-quality targets; the paper's about-30-dB planned cabled switch path requires a transmit retimer, while its CPO path is below 12 dB.
exact_wording: The linear LPO needs 22 dB loss to meet the 200G RX sensitivity requirement ... CPO has <12dB loss
comparison_baseline: A universal 200G LPO electrical-loss limit
independent_support: The paper specifies 113 GBd PAM4, concatenated KP4/Hamming FEC, 500 m CWDM4 and the modeled channel context.
contradicting_evidence: Simulation rather than measured link; result is conditional on FEC, loss allocation, transmitter/receiver and equalisation assumptions.
notes: Use as a conservative topology trigger, not a vendor-neutral LPO specification.

claim: PAP-007 reports 20 pJ/bit for a fully retimed 100G module and 12.5 pJ/bit for its LPO case, but the paper's 5-10 pJ/bit CPO range is cited from another source and the paper does not establish a matched full-system power boundary.
exact_wording: the power consumption of a 100G module can be reduced by 37% from 20 pJ/bit to 12.5 pJ/bit
comparison_baseline: Measured 102.4T CPO-versus-LPO system or chassis power
independent_support: The text explicitly states the 100G module comparison and separately attributes the CPO range to a cited reference.
contradicting_evidence: Module/system inclusions, samples, temperature and workload are not fully reconciled; CPO number is not a matched direct measurement in this paper.
notes: Supports directionally lower LPO power versus retiming but must not replace the 102.4T scenario-model inputs.

claim: Hisense's VPI model reports that a 200G/lane TFLN design at 31 dB electrical-channel loss produces 2.1 dB TDECQ, 3.1 dB extinction ratio and -4.5 dBm receiver OMA with a model-limited BER below 1e-6 when enhanced transmitter CTLE is used.
exact_wording: At 31dB loss, the TDECQ can be 2.1dB, ER 3.1dB, and RxOMA -4.5dBm
comparison_baseline: Measured 200G/lane module or system link
independent_support: The paper identifies VPI simulation, 112 GBd PAM4, 90 GHz TFLN MZM, transmitter peaking and host equalisation assumptions.
contradicting_evidence: No direct link measurement; authors state the simulation needs an improved model below 1e-6 BER.
notes: 31 dB is an architecture-model result, not an independently established LPO reach limit.

claim: PAP-008 does not establish that its SiP alternative can equal the modeled TFLN 31-dB result: the SiP path has a reported BER floor above 1e-5 in the body, while the conclusion describes a 1e-4 result, and neither is a measured complete link.
exact_wording: BER floor > 1E-5 ... BER reaches 1E-4 for SiP
comparison_baseline: A precise technology ranking between SiP and TFLN at 200G/lane
independent_support: The paper describes lower SiP modulator and driver bandwidth than the TFLN case and reports poorer simulated BER behaviour.
contradicting_evidence: Internal wording is inconsistent and both paths are modeled; no statistical device, power, yield or link measurement is supplied.
notes: Treat SiP as poorer/unresolved in this source, not as a quantified head-to-head commercial result.

claim: The 22/23 dB, 26 dB and 31 dB 200G LPO loss results in PAP-007, PAP-010 and PAP-008 cannot be used to rank architectures or reliability because their channel, frequency, FEC, return-loss, transmitter, modulator and equalisation assumptions differ.
comparison_baseline: A matched 200G/lane loss-budget and reliability comparison
independent_support: Each paper specifies a materially different simulation or design boundary and none supplies a common measured multi-vendor system.
contradicting_evidence: An undiscovered matched test could reconcile the results; this inference does not imply that all designs perform equally.
notes: Do not average or select the largest loss figure as an LPO capability rule.

claim: Semtech's less-than-10-W 1.6T LPO figure is an internal simulation of TIA and driver power plus realistic estimates for laser and ancillary power, while its 20-25 W fully retimed figures are stated technology-node expectations rather than a matched measurement.
exact_wording: Based on internal simulation ... a 1.6T LPO module should require less than 10W
comparison_baseline: Measured 1.6T LPO versus retimed module power at the same reach and conditions
independent_support: The paper labels the LPO figure as internal simulation and estimates and frames retimed values as future 2 nm/3 nm expectations.
contradicting_evidence: No sample, measurement boundary, module thermal state, laser specification or independent validation is provided.
notes: Use as a stress-boundary reference only; it is not an input upgrade for the 102.4T power model.

claim: Semtech's 200G model reaches BER below 1e-6 at 26 dB die-to-die loss only with its stated host equalisation and better-than-10-dB return-loss boundary; the authors report that a 200G multi-channel-board test was difficult because of reflections.
exact_wording: BER can be corrected to below 1E-6 with 15 taps FFE ... reflection is the biggest concern
comparison_baseline: Measured 200G multi-vendor switch-channel performance
independent_support: The paper provides its PRBS, bandwidth, FFE/DFE, loss and return-loss model parameters and discusses measurement difficulty.
contradicting_evidence: The claimed result is modeled, and no full 200G production switch test or BER distribution across ports is reported.
notes: Supports return loss and host equalisation as essential diligence fields.

claim: PAP-010's statement that 100G LPO entered initial production across a 64-port switch with BER floors of 1e-12 and 1e-9 is indirect cited evidence, not a named-customer or independently documented production record in the reviewed paper.
exact_wording: LPO began initial production deployment in a 64 port switch ... error floors of 1E-12 and 1E-9
comparison_baseline: Customer-confirmed 100G LPO deployment and field reliability
independent_support: The paper reports the claim and cites an earlier source.
contradicting_evidence: No named system, customer, duration, units, service or field error statistics are supplied in PAP-010 itself.
notes: Do not count this as independent production evidence without reviewing the underlying cited source and customer confirmation.

claim: PAP-011 directly measures 160 and 180 GBd PAM4 component performance, but does not directly measure the 212.5 GBd PAM4 rate needed for its modeled 400G/lane implementation or an end-to-end 400G link.
exact_wording: We have demonstrated 160 GBd and 180 GBd PAM4 performance ... 400G/lane signal is simulated
comparison_baseline: Measured 400G/lane linear-drive system result
independent_support: The paper separates the laboratory measurement section from a VPI 212.5 GBd simulation section.
contradicting_evidence: Measured component TDECQ/BER boundary is not a 400G link, fibre reach, multi-lane module or production result.
notes: Critical distinction for CPO/NPO timing claims.

claim: In PAP-011's 212.5 GBd PAM4/KP4 model, TDECQ below 3.5 dB and BER floor below 1e-6 hold only up to 12 dB back-to-back loss at 106 GHz; at 15 dB, the model reports 6.5 dB TDECQ and BER worse than 1e-5.
exact_wording: the 12dB channel loss can achieve ... TDECQ < 3.5dB and BER floor < 1E-6
comparison_baseline: Measured 400G/lane electrical-loss tolerance
independent_support: The paper specifies the 212.5 GBd simulation, 9 dB CTLE, channel loss and comparison conditions.
contradicting_evidence: Model result only; no demonstrated 212.5 GBd link, thermal distribution, manufacturing tolerance, fibre reach or serviceability evidence.
notes: Supports a short NPO/CPO electrical path direction, not established conventional 400G LPO.

claim: The reviewed PAP-007, PAP-008, PAP-010 and PAP-011 set does not provide a measured, multi-vendor 200G/lane system or a measured end-to-end 400G/lane linear-drive system at a common electrical-loss, return-loss, FEC, reach, temperature, power and reliability boundary.
comparison_baseline: Commercial deployment or architecture-leadership conclusion
independent_support: The review distinguishes Meta's 100G experiment, the 200G simulations/design studies and the 400G component measurement plus simulation.
contradicting_evidence: Other papers or non-public customer evidence may exist; absence in this set is not evidence of impossibility.
notes: Primary gap before assigning LPO, NPO or CPO adoption timing or profit-pool leadership.

claim: Coherent says its OFC 2026 CPO demonstrations include a 6.4T socketed silicon-photonics system with 32 x 200G lanes and an external laser source, a VCSEL CPO system, and a 400G-per-lane InP modulator array on silicon.
exact_wording: Demonstrations include a 6.4T (32×200G) socketed CPO ... and an InP modulator on silicon operating at 400G
comparison_baseline: Qualified production 200G/400G scale-out optical engine
independent_support: The company specifies the architectures and lane/aggregate figures in an OFC announcement.
contradicting_evidence: Company demonstration; no stated customer, complete link/power/thermal boundary, yield, qualification, field reliability or commercial unit volume.
notes: Useful breadth evidence, not a company-leadership or profit conclusion.

claim: Coherent states that its first six-inch InP line is in volume production and that it plans total InP-output expansion in both 2026 and 2027, but the disclosure does not specify CPO-engine capacity, yield, allocation or customer qualification.
exact_wording: First 6” InP line in volume production ... Production doubling in 2026 and 2027
comparison_baseline: CPO optical-engine manufacturing readiness
independent_support: The company investor material identifies the line, facilities and planned expansion timeline.
contradicting_evidence: Capacity statement is company supplied and covers InP output broadly; it does not show final-engine conversion, CPO allocation, fibre-attach/test throughput, yield or shipped volume.

contradicting_evidence: A Huawei standards contribution is not IEEE consensus or a ratified specification; it gives no link measurements, test points, interoperable product, qualification, cost or volume evidence.
